title: Volumes & Networks in Compose
subtitle: Explicit network segmentation, named volumes, and multi-service data sharing patterns

content.text: By default, all services in a Compose file share one network — every service can reach every other. For production-style security, you create explicit networks and attach only the services that need to communicate. A frontend and database should never share a network.

content.code:
services:

  # nginx reverse proxy — on both networks so it can route traffic
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    networks:
      - frontend
      - backend
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf

  # API server — only on backend network
  api:
    build: .
    networks:
      - backend
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:secret@db:5432/myapp

  # Database — only on backend network (never reachable from frontend)
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    networks:
      - backend
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

# Define networks explicitly
networks:
  frontend:
    driver: bridge
  backend:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  db-data:

services:
  app:
    image: myapp
    volumes:
      # Bind mount — great for dev hot-reload
      - ./src:/app/src
      # Named volume — persistent data
      - app-data:/app/data
      # Read-only bind mount — config file
      - ./config.json:/app/config.json:ro
      # Shared volume between two services
      - shared-uploads:/app/uploads

  worker:
    image: myworker
    volumes:
      # Same named volume — both services access the same uploads
      - shared-uploads:/worker/uploads

volumes:
  app-data:
    # driver options for custom storage backends
    driver: local
  shared-uploads:
    # External volume: must exist before compose up
    # external: true
    # name: my-existing-volume

content.text: Compose override files — dev vs prod

content.code:
# docker-compose.yml — base (shared between dev and prod)
# docker-compose.override.yml — auto-loaded in development
# docker-compose.prod.yml — explicit production overrides

# docker-compose.yml (base)
services:
  api:
    image: myapp-api
    environment:
      PORT: 3000

---
# docker-compose.override.yml (dev additions — auto-merged)
services:
  api:
    build: .
    volumes:
      - ./src:/app/src   # hot reload
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: development
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"

---
# docker-compose.prod.yml (production)
services:
  api:
    image: ghcr.io/myorg/api:1.4.2
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m

# Development (auto-merges docker-compose.override.yml)
docker compose up -d

# Production (explicitly specify files)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

questions.question: You have 'api' and 'database' services. You define two networks: 'frontend' and 'backend'. You put 'api' on both, 'database' only on 'backend'. Can database reach api?
options: No — database is only on backend and api straddles both networks
Yes — they share the backend network, so they can communicate
No — services can only communicate on the frontend network
Only if you add -p to the database service
questions.explanation: Both services share the 'backend' network, so they can communicate with each other using their service names as hostnames. 'api' can reach 'database' at 'database:5432'. The frontend network is just for nginx-to-api traffic. Network membership is checked per network — if two services share ANY network, they can communicate.

faq.q: What happens to named volumes when I run docker compose down?
faq.a: Named volumes are preserved by default — 'docker compose down' stops and removes containers but keeps volumes. Your database data survives. To also delete volumes, run 'docker compose down -v' — but this permanently deletes all data in named volumes. Never run -v without knowing what data you're destroying.

examples: Monorepos with separate frontend/backend services use network segmentation in Compose so the React dev server can't directly query the database
Two workers processing uploaded files use a shared named volume so file-upload service and thumbnail-generator service both access /uploads
